Why work with us:
At Shifted Designs, we strive to shift the way we think, operate, and design. We're a growing civil engineering consultancy focused on delivering practical, innovative and sustainable solutions across a diverse range of projects.
Our team values collaboration, initiative and continuous improvement. In return, we offer a supportive workplace, opportunities for professional growth, exposure to varied and rewarding projects, and a genuine chance to help shape the future of our business.

We are seeking an experienced Civil Designer to produce detailed civil engineering designs and drawing packages using AutoCAD and Civil 3D. You will work closely with engineers and project managers on a range of residential, commercial and industrial developments, helping deliver high-quality design solutions from concept through to construction documentation.

- Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a collaborative team environment.

- Prepare detailed civil engineering designs and documentation for a range of residential, commercial and industrial development projects.
- Produce high-quality construction drawings, plans and supporting documentation.
- Use AutoCAD and Civil 3D to prepare detailed and precise civil drawings for earthworks, road, drainage and subdivision design.
- Develop and maintain Civil 3D models, surfaces, pipe networks and design data.
- Interpret and coordinate information from architectural, structural, electrical, hydraulic and other consultant drawings.
- Liaise closely with engineers and project managers to deliver practical and cost-effective design solutions.
- Ensure all drawings and documentation comply with company standards, relevant Australian Standards and client requirements.

content_text:
At City of Newcastle (CN), you won't just design roads, drainage networks, cycleways and recreational infrastructure, you'll help create the places where our community lives, works and connects. This is an exciting opportunity to bring your technical expertise, creativity and project management skills to a role that delivers lasting outcomes for one of Australia's most vibrant and evolving cities.
As a member of our team, you won't just work for the city; you’ll co-create it. Here, your ideas and efforts directly shape the places where you and your community live, work, and play.
We currently have two permanent Civil Designer opportunities available within our team.
As a Civil Designer, you will take a lead role in the design and delivery of a diverse range of civil infrastructure projects. From initial investigations and concept development through to detailed design, approvals and construction support, you will be responsible for producing high-quality design documentation that transforms ideas into community assets.
Working collaboratively across the organisation and with external stakeholders, you will manage the design process, coordinate consultants and contractors, and oversee project budgets through the design and approval phases. You will provide technical advice during construction, work through complex design challenges and help ensure projects are delivered safely, sustainably and cost-effectively.
This role offers the opportunity to influence the future of Newcastle by delivering infrastructure that improves connectivity, enhances public spaces and supports a growing city. You'll apply your expertise to project investigations, design development, cost estimates, environmental assessments and planning approvals while ensuring compliance with relevant standards, legislation and best-practice design principles.
Beyond project delivery, you'll play an important role in strengthening capability across the team by sharing your knowledge, supporting less experienced designers and contributing to innovation and continuous improvement. You'll help foster a collaborative environment where safety, excellence and creative problem-solving are valued and encouraged.
We're looking for motivated and forward-thinking professionals who combine strong technical design skills with the ability to build relationships, manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality outcomes. Through your work, you’ll have a behind the scenes pass to Newcastle's evolution as you shape our future as a liveable, inclusive city.
Life at City of Newcastle (CN) 
You’ll get to experience your work up close alongside the brilliant minds of your colleagues who care for one another and the region.
You’ll chip away at ambitious plans with a talented, passionate crew alongside you, shaping the very fabric of our community. Showing up for neighbours not shareholders.
Every single day offers the chance to think big and act local. Planning and prioritising to achieve the most important outcomes with the community.
You’ll add value in the moments that matter. From librarians to lifeguards, in a range of iconic places, we achieve a better Newcastle together.
Whether we’re planning to host major events, providing essential services or supporting creative artists, it’s what we do when the cameras aren't rolling that matters most.
And we’ll be there for you in important times in your life. We embrace flexible work arrangements to find a balance that allows us to enjoy the city we shape.
Our focus on inclusion and respecting culture, will help you feel a deeper connection with others. You'll connect with internal communities that will help you to feel a sense of belonging and reflect the diversity of the growing region.
You’ll do meaningful work and do it sustainably as you take ideas from plan to play, in your own backyard.
With hundreds of different roles, each person adds their uniqueness to our culture and plays their part as we head towards our 2040 vision.
With natural assets and a focus on the environment, co-create a sustainable region with us.
Why join CN? 
At CN, we value our employees, and their wellbeing takes priority. We encourage employees to make time for what's important and provide the benefits to enable a work life balance that allow us to enjoy the city we shape. To read more, visit here!

- Access to a range of exclusive CN employee benefits programs including Novated Lease options as well as access to reward and recognition vouchers

- Leading the CN Way leadership program
- Inclusion, Diversity & Equity (IDE) employee networks and initiatives
- Access to Health & Wellbeing programs including an Onsite Physiotherapist and Psychology, Yoga and Mental Health Ambassador Groups
We champion inclusion so that everyone is valued, and we encourage innovation and creativity. We are committed to creating a safe and inclusive workplace where different styles, backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives are valued, encouraged, and respected.
People with diverse lived experiences (including but not limited to, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians, people with diverse gender identities and sexualities, people from different cultural, racial, ethnic, religious and linguistic backgrounds, people with disability, carers, and veterans) are encouraged to apply.
Don’t just work for the city, co-create it. Join and expand your career at the City of Newcastle.

content_text:
Civil Designer (Ref: 1350)
About the position:
The Civil Designer prepares concept and detailed designs, drawings, quantity schedules, cost estimates, and supporting technical documentation for the City’s capital works and infrastructure programs. The role undertakes investigations and design development for transport, parks and open space, and utility infrastructure assets, ensuring designs are safe, practical, constructable, maintainable, compliant and fit for purpose. Working under general direction, the position provides technical design advice, contributes to project scoping and option assessment, liaises with internal and external stakeholders to obtain design inputs, and maintains accurate design and handover records.
Key accountabilities:
- Review project briefs and available asset, survey, geotechnical, environmental and service information to identify information gaps. Undertake site inspections and engineering investigations, and develop an appropriate design approach, program and estimate of design effort.
- Prepare concept and detailed designs for municipal infrastructure including earthworks, roads, intersections, roundabouts, car parks, footpaths, shared paths, kerbing, stormwater drainage, culverts and associated civil works, using the City’s approved design and drafting systems.
- Prepare and document relevant design calculations, drawings, schedules of quantities, cost estimates, technical specifications, design reports, approvals information and other documentation required for grant applications, procurement and construction.
For further information and to view the position description, visit www.cgg.wa.gov.au/employment/.
To gain a better understanding of the role, please call Trevor Pitt, Coordinator Design on (08) 9956 6650.
Position requirements:
The successful applicant will ideally hold a Degree in Civil Engineering. Applicants with lesser qualification but significant experience in the design and drafting of reads, footpaths, drainage and other minor scale civil infrastructure works will also be considered. Experience in writing grant applications would be highly regarded.
Completion of a pre-employment medical including alcohol and other substances testing is required of all positions at the City.
Remuneration and benefits:
This position offers a salary starting from $92,692 per annum or $104,203 per hour, commensurate with the successful applicant’s knowledge, skills, experience and qualifications.
Some of the additional benefits of working for the City include:
- Up to 21% Superannuation (with superannuation co-contribution scheme)
- 22 Annual Leave days per annum
- Health & Wellbeing Program
- Flexible working arrangements
- Career opportunities
- Study Assistance
- Centrally located
- Free parking
About the City
Overlooking the Indian Ocean, Geraldton is a thriving regional city at the heart of Australia's Coral Coast. With a growing population of over 41,000 people it offers a wide range of services and activities. Geraldton is recognised as one of WA's key growth areas and the opportunities in this regional city are plentiful. You can be part of working with us to deliver the best for our community and this region.
The City of Greater Geraldton actively welcomes, includes and values the unique contributions of all people in its workplace. The City welcomes applications from all age groups, people with a disability, and those from diverse ethnic and cultural backgrounds. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer with strong commitment to fitness for work and safety in the workplace.
Interested in applying?
Visit the City’s website: www.cgg.wa.gov.au/employment/ to apply for this position.
To be considered for this vacancy, applicants are advised to include the following:
- A current resume
- A written response (maximum 1250 characters per criteria) addressing the following selection criteria inclusive of examples to support your claims:
i. Degree in Civil Engineering, Diploma in Civil Construction Design, Civil Engineering, Civil and Structural Engineering, or lesser relevant discipline qualifications and substantial civil design experience
ii. Demonstrated competency in relevant civil design and drafting software, including 12d Model and AutoCAD and/or Civil 3D, with demonstrated ability to become proficient in the City’s adopted systems
iii. Demonstrated experience preparing civil engineering designs and drawings for roads, intersections, footpaths, drainage, carparks and related municipal infrastructure
iv. Knowledge of Austroads, Main Roads WA requirements, Australian Rainfall and Runoff, Australian Standards water sensitive urban design and utility coordination
v. High level emotional intelligence, negotiation, problem solving and conflict resolution skills to enable effective liaison with all people at all levels and to persuade others to adopt particular methods or strategies where there are conflicting interests and opinions

We are looking for Site and Project Engineers with experience across bulk earthworks, subdivisions/land development, renewable energy projects including solar and wind, roads or heavy civil infrastructure.

Project Engineers will take broader ownership across planning, commercial management, procurement, programming and client coordination.

- Build and maintain strong client and stakeholder relationships

- Demonstrated experience in bulk earthworks and/or subdivisions
- Experience with self-performing civil contractors highly regarded
- Solar, wind or other renewable infrastructure experience highly regarded

- Strong understanding of construction methods, specifications and project delivery
- Confident working directly with Supervisors, Surveyors and field crews
- Proficient in Microsoft Office and Project Management systems
- Proactive, detail-focused and able to take ownership of works
- White Card and current Australian Driver Licence
What We Offer
- Competitive salary + vehicle
- Living away from home allowance (for eligible employees working away from home), flights and accommodation covered on swing
- 10/4 roster – providing work/life balance
- Exposure to diverse and challenging civil projects
- Supportive team environment with strong leadership
- Career development and progression opportunities
- Opportunity to move between regional projects
How to Apply
If you are ready to take the next step in your career with a company that values your expertise, apply now by submitting your CV and cover letter.
If you would like to chat about the role, contact Monica Stoddard, HR Officer, on monica@aoneearthworks.com.au
We are an equal opportunity employer and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds.

content_text:
About Us
Exclusive Construction Machinery and Equipment Pty Ltd is a dynamic and growing civil construction and earthmoving business operating in Western Australia. We specialise in comprehensive earthworks, site preparation, and civil projects that support residential, commercial, and industrial developments. Our projects involve excavation, land clearing, bulk earthworks, trenching, drainage preparation and other essential groundwork that form the critical foundation for infrastructure and building works across the region. Our team works with a modern fleet of machinery and experienced operators to deliver high-quality results safely, efficiently, and on schedule.
Role Overview
We are seeking a motivated Civil Engineering Technician to provide comprehensive technical support to our Civil Engineer across multiple earthworks and site-development projects in Western Australia.
The successful candidate will assist in collecting and analysing site data, preparing and updating engineering drawings, checking completed earthworks against approved drawings and specifications, calculating construction quantities, and preparing technical records and reports. The role combines office-based technical drafting and documentation with regular site attendance for field measurements, construction material testing, technical inspections and quality verification. It supports the accurate implementation and verification of civil engineering works in accordance with approved designs, relevant Australian Standards, project specifications and applicable WHS requirements.
Key Responsibilities
- Assist Civil Engineers in preparing, interpreting and revising civil engineering sketches, technical drawings, plans and technical details for earthworks, site preparation, excavation, trenching and drainage works using AutoCAD and Civil 3D, based on engineering instructions, site measurements and approved design information.
- Prepare and update as-built drawings, drawing registers and associated technical documentation using AutoCAD and Civil 3D to reflect verified site conditions, completed civil engineering works and approved design changes.
- Undertake field measurements and collect site data relating to ground levels, excavation dimensions, earthworks profiles, drainage gradients and site formation to support civil engineering construction activities.
- Analyse and compare field measurements and survey data against approved engineering drawings, design levels, project specifications and applicable technical requirements, identify discrepancies and prepare technical data for review by the Civil Engineer.
- Assist in conducting and coordinating field and laboratory tests of soil and other construction materials, as required, recording results and analysing available test data against project specifications and acceptance criteria.
- Conduct technical inspections of earthworks, excavation, trenching, drainage preparation and site-formation activities, assess completed works against approved drawings and engineering specifications, and document discrepancies and non-conformances for review and rectification.
- Monitor soil placement, filling, backfilling, compaction and drainage works by reviewing field measurements and available material test results, checking completed works against specified engineering requirements and reporting deviations for further assessment.
- Perform technical computations using site measurements, survey information, engineering drawings and relevant technical data to calculate and verify earthworks quantities, excavation and fill volumes, cut-and-fill requirements and construction material quantities.
- Prepare material quantity schedules, earthworks quantity summaries, technical tabulations and supporting tender documentation, and assist in estimating material and labour quantities and costs using engineering drawings, site measurements and relevant construction data.
- Compile and analyse field measurements, survey data, material testing results and inspection findings, and prepare technical reports, data sheets, charts, tabulations, inspection checklists and compliance records for review by the Civil Engineer.
- Check subcontractor drawings, method statements, technical submissions and construction documentation against approved engineering drawings, project specifications and applicable contract requirements, identify technical discrepancies and refer matters requiring engineering judgement or approval to the Civil Engineer.
- Interpret civil engineering work instructions and communicate technical site information, measurement requirements and relevant engineering specifications to site supervisors, machinery operators, subcontractors, surveyors and other project personnel to support the accurate implementation and verification of civil engineering works.
- Maintain accurate technical records of engineering drawings, field measurements, material testing results, inspection findings and project documentation to support technical verification, quality control, compliance reviews and construction handover.
- Identify and document site conditions and technical issues that may affect the quality or compliance of civil engineering construction works, and promptly report discrepancies and matters requiring further technical assessment to the Civil Engineer.
Skills & Qualifications Required
- Diploma or Advanced Diploma in Civil Engineering, Civil Construction, Building Engineering Technology, or a closely related civil engineering or construction technology discipline. Applicants with other relevant qualifications and substantial, directly relevant civil engineering technical experience may also be considered.
- Minimum 2 years of relevant experience in civil engineering technical support, earthworks, site preparation, drainage works or civil construction.
- Working knowledge of relevant Australian Standards and project specifications applicable to earthworks, soil testing, compaction and site development, including AS 3798 and relevant parts of the AS 1289 series, where applicable.
- Practical competency in AutoCAD and Civil 3D for preparing and updating civil engineering drawings and as-built documentation.
- Ability to interpret civil engineering drawings and specifications, undertake site measurements, record field data and assist with earthworks quantity calculations.
- Understanding of technical inspections, construction quality control, field reporting and documentation of non-conformances.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word. Working knowledge of MS Project is desirable.
- Strong communication and coordination skills when working with Civil Engineers, surveyors, site supervisors, subcontractors and machinery operators.
- Current White Card (Construction Induction Safety Certificate), or willingness and ability to obtain it before commencing site work, where required.
- Valid Australian driver licence, or the ability to obtain an appropriate licence before commencing duties requiring driving, and willingness to travel between project sites across Western Australia as required.
Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, permanent
- Salary: $80,000-90,000 per annum plus superannuation, depending on experience
- Benefits: Travel reimbursement
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shifts, Monday to Friday
What We Offer
- Competitive salary package plus superannuation
- Stable, long-term permanent employment opportunity
- Opportunities for career progression, training and professional development while working alongside experienced Civil Engineers
- Visa sponsorship under the Subclass 482 Skills in Demand visa program may be available to suitably qualified applicants who meet the relevant immigration requirements
- Supportive team culture and modern work systems
- Full personal protective equipment (PPE) and relevant work equipment provided to support role performance
How to Apply
Please click Apply Now to submit your updated resume. Applicants should highlight their relevant civil engineering technical experience, qualifications, software competency and current Australian work rights or visa status.
Shortlisted candidates will be contacted for a confidential interview.

Help shape stormwater’s next chapter.
You’ve built your technical skills. You’re ready to take on more responsibility, contribute your ideas and develop the confidence to lead.
Rain Consulting is looking for a Project Engineer or Scientist with 3 to 7 years’ relevant experience to join our Melbourne team.
We’re a specialist stormwater and surface water consultancy. We plan and design better water environments, investigate how water behaves and help clients turn complex information into decisions they can act on.
Our purpose
At Rain, we exist to support, challenge and lift ourselves, each other and the people we work with.
That means helping clients understand their options and giving them the clarity and confidence to act. It also means backing our own people to develop their judgement, take ownership and contribute to how the industry works.
We value creative thinking, especially when it leads to a sound, practical solution.
How we work
Our values guide our decisions and the standards we hold ourselves to:
- Quality: We check assumptions, review our work and explain the findings clearly.
- Integrity: We give honest advice, including when a client needs to hear something difficult.
- Stewardship: We consider what our decisions mean for communities and the environment over the long term.
You’ll work with major clients, including City of Melbourne and Melbourne Water, as part of a small team where your contribution is visible.
You’ll have direct support from Luke and Rianda, Rain’s Directors, and colleagues who want to see you develop. As your capability grows, there’s room to take on greater responsibility and build your own voice in the industry.
We welcome questions, thoughtful challenges and ideas for doing things better. You’ll be trusted to contribute, with technical review and support around you.
The role is Melbourne-based with hybrid working and flexibility, within a team that looks out for each other.
The problems you’ll help solve
A council is rethinking how it manages water across its community. A wetland or waterway needs a design that supports both people and the environment. A project needs a water balance to understand where water comes from, where it goes and how it could be used.
And behind each challenge, there are people who need help turning complex information into a clear way forward.
These are the kinds of questions you’ll work through at Rain.
You’ll use TUFLOW and RORB to investigate how water behaves, test options and understand their consequences. Your projects may also involve wetland and waterway design, water balances and integrated water management. You’ll turn that work into clear maps, reports and conversations that help people make sound decisions.
You’ll also get involved beyond the technical analysis. From shaping the brief to discussing the findings with the client, you’ll develop an understanding of what makes a project useful, achievable and worth doing. That includes managing scope, budgets and deadlines, with support from the team.
We want you to question assumptions and contribute ideas. If you see a better way to approach a problem, explain a result or manage water, there’s room to explore it with us.
As your confidence and capability grow, you’ll have opportunities to take greater ownership, guide others and contribute to our training or facilitation work.
The aim is for your contribution to keep helping people long after the report is delivered.
What you’ll bring
- An Engineering degree, including civil or environmental engineering, or an Environmental Science degree.
- 3 to 7 years’ relevant experience in flood, stormwater or water management.
- Solid practical TUFLOW and RORB skills.
- An understanding of hydrologic, hydraulic and stormwater processes.
- The ability to plan your work, take responsibility and ask for support when you need it.
- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain technical findings to different audiences.
- Curiosity about better ways of doing things and care for the quality and impact of your work.
Experience with MUSIC and QGIS is valuable. Training, facilitation or mentoring experience is a bonus.
Your next move
Send your CV and a short note about why you’d like to work at Rain to hiring@rainconsulting.com.au.
Tell us about the work you’ve done, the work you’d like to do next and what you’d bring to the team.
You’re also welcome to email us if you’d like to ask a question before applying.
We welcome applications from people with different backgrounds and experiences.

GRADUATE / JUNIOR ESTIMATOR – COMMERCIAL CONSTRUCTION
Cairns, QLD | Full-Time | Graduate / Entry Level
WIP Construction is looking for a motivated Graduate or Junior Estimator to join our Cairns-based team. This is an office-based position located in Cairns, Queensland. Applicants must be based in Cairns or willing to relocate.
This is an opportunity for someone who wants to build a career in commercial construction estimating. You don't need previous experience as an Estimator, we're more interested in finding someone with the right aptitude, attitude and genuine desire to learn.
You may be a recent graduate, currently studying, or at the beginning of your construction career and looking for an opportunity to develop practical, hands-on experience within an established commercial construction company.
The Role
Working alongside our experienced estimating and project team, you'll learn how commercial construction projects are priced, tendered and ultimately delivered.
As your experience develops, you'll be involved in:
- Reviewing construction drawings, specifications and tender documentation
- Assisting with quantity take-offs and pricing
- Preparing and issuing subcontractor and supplier enquiries
- Reviewing and comparing quotations
- Assisting with tender submissions
- Understanding project scope, methodology and construction requirements
- Building relationships with subcontractors and suppliers
- Working with our project delivery team to understand how estimates translate into live projects
- Developing your knowledge of commercial construction costs, trades and procurement
We don't expect you to know how to do all of this on day one. We'll teach you.
What we do expect is that you genuinely want to learn.
We're looking for someone who is curious, switched-on and interested in understanding how and why things are built and what they cost.
You may be studying or have recently completed a qualification in:
- Construction Management
- Quantity Surveying
- Civil Engineering
- Building & Construction
- Project Management
- Engineering
- Or another relevant construction-related discipline
We're also open to applicants from other backgrounds who can demonstrate strong numerical, analytical and problem-solving skills and a genuine interest in pursuing a career in construction estimating.
Previous estimating experience is not required.
More important to us is someone who:
- Has strong numerical and analytical skills
- Has excellent attention to detail
- Can read information carefully and ask questions when something doesn't make sense
- Is organised and able to manage competing priorities
- Communicates confidently and professionally
- Takes ownership of their work
- Has a genuine interest in building a long-term career in commercial construction
WIP Construction is an established Cairns-based commercial construction company delivering projects throughout Cairns and Far North Queensland.
You'll be joining a team where you'll have the opportunity to learn from experienced construction professionals and gain exposure to real commercial projects from tender through to delivery.
This isn't a graduate role where you'll spend months watching from the sidelines.
You'll be given real work, real responsibility and plenty of support while you develop your skills.
For the right person, there is significant opportunity to grow within the business and develop into an experienced Estimator.
If you're motivated, good with numbers, interested in construction and looking for somewhere to start your career, we'd like to hear from you.
Apply through SEEK with your resume and a short cover letter telling us a little about yourself, what you're currently studying or have completed, and why estimating and commercial construction interests you.
teaser: Kickstart your career in construction estimating! No experience required, just a great attitude and willingness to learn.

Kickstart Your Career in Engineering Drafting! 
Ready to turn your interest in design and engineering into a career? 
Whether you’re finishing Year 12, recently left school or studying Drafting at TAFE, this is your opportunity to get started in the engineering industry. 
STP Consultants is looking for an enthusiastic Junior Structural Draftsperson to join our growing Brisbane team. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers and drafters, gain hands-on experience and learn how the drawings you create become part of real projects across Queensland. 
You don’t need years of experience. We’re looking for someone with the right attitude, curiosity and willingness to learn. 
Why you’ll love working here 
Start building your career   Get hands-on experience from day one and develop practical Structural drafting skills while learning from experienced engineers and drafters. 
Work on real projects   Go beyond the classroom and see how structural engineering projects come together. You’ll contribute to drawings and documentation used throughout projects from concept and design through to delivery. 
Learn from experienced people   Ask questions, share ideas and learn from people who genuinely want to help you develop. You’ll receive guidance and mentoring as your skills and confidence grow. 
Be part of a great team   Join a close-knit, collaborative team where people support each other, work together and enjoy what they do. 
Work in Fortitude Valley   Our Brisbane office is in the heart of Fortitude Valley, close to public transport, cafés, restaurants and everything the city has to offer.
The Opportunity  
As you develop your skills, you’ll have the opportunity to: 
- Assist with preparing structural drawings, plans and project documentation. 
- Work with engineers and experienced drafters to produce clear, accurate and high-quality drawings. 
- Learn industry standards, guidelines and best-practice drafting processes. 
- Develop your understanding of how structural engineering projects are designed and delivered. 
- Participate in project discussions and meetings to build your understanding of project requirements. 
- Carry out basic drawing and documentation checks with guidance from experienced team members. 
- Take on more responsibility as your skills and confidence develop. 
About you: 
You could be a great fit if you are: 
- A Year 12 student, recent school leaver, or currently studying Residential Drafting, or an equivalent qualification at TAFE.
- Genuinely interested in structural drafting, design and engineering. 
- Curious and keen to learn new skills. 
- Detail-oriented and take pride in producing accurate work. 
- A good communicator who is comfortable asking questions and taking feedback. 
- Reliable, organised and willing to have a go at new challenges. 
- Someone who enjoys working with others and being part of a team. 
- An Australian Citizen or Permanent Resident. 
Most importantly, bring your enthusiasm and willingness to learn. We’ll help you turn it into a career. 
What’s in it for you? 
- 
Career development: Build your skills through hands-on experience, mentoring and ongoing professional development. 
- 
Flexibility: Enjoy a 9-day fortnight, flexible working hours and the option to purchase additional leave. 
- 
Competitive remuneration: A package that reflects your experience and contribution. 
- 
Recognition and rewards: Employee referral rewards and recognition programs. 
- 
Great culture: Work with supportive people in a friendly, collaborative environment, with regular team and social events. 
- 
Wellbeing support: Access to a confidential Employee Assistance Program. 
- 
Long-term opportunity: Build your career with an established, Australian-owned engineering consultancy. 
About STP Consultants  
For more than 20 years, STP Consultants has been helping shape communities across Queensland. 
We’re a privately owned, multidisciplinary engineering consultancy, bringing together expertise across Civil, Structural, Mechanical, Electrical, Hydraulic, Fire and Seismic engineering. Our teams work on a diverse range of projects across Queensland, giving you the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals and see the many different paths an engineering career can take. 
Our values of Potential, Respect, Integrity, Deliver and Engage shape the way we work with our clients and with each other. 
We’re proud of our approachable leaders, supportive team environment and commitment to developing people and delivering quality engineering outcomes. 
Ready to get started?   
If you’re looking for more than just a first job and want to build a career in engineering, we’d love to hear from you. 
Click Apply and send us your Resume and Cover Letter. 
In your cover letter, tell us: 
1. Why you’re interested in starting a career in structural drafting.   
2. What interests you about joining STP Consultants. 
STP Consultants is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and welcome applications from all backgrounds.

Mildura Rural City Council is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to building a culture that values diversity. We encourage applications from individuals of all ages, backgrounds and identities.
We encourage people with a disability, lived experience of disability, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders and people from culturally diverse backgrounds to apply for this position.

Mildura Rural City Council is a Child Safe organisation and as such, applicants may be required to hold a Working with Children Check. Applicants may also be required to undergo a pre-employment medical check as per the requirements of the role.
About our organisation
Mildura Rural City Council is a dynamic local government organisation that provides 100+ different services, facilities, programs and infrastructure to a resident base of 56,000+. As an employer of choice and a Gold Award winner in the Business Excellence Awards, we are committed to innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement. Mildura Rural City covers almost 10 per cent of the state of Victoria and shares borders with both New South Wales and South Australia. The region is home to Mildura - a vibrant city of 35,000+ people - and a range of smaller townships and rural communities spread across 22,000 square kilometres.
Only a short flight from three capital cities, Mildura boasts quality services, exciting attractions, diverse industries and a strong community spirit. There are fantastic professional, cultural, social, sporting and educational opportunities on offer. Learn more about our region at www.visitmildura.com.au

content_text:
Westera Partners is a leading consulting engineering firm with offices across Queensland, New South Wales, and Victoria. We not only deliver high-quality, value-driven civil, structural, and environmental solutions — we’re equally recognised for the way we look after people —both our clients and our team. We pride ourselves on building trusted relationships, fostering professional growth, and creating a workplace where excellence and collaboration are pillars of our long-standing success.
The Opportunity
Due to increasing demand for our services, we are looking for a highly motivated Civil Design Engineer with at least 7 years of experience to join our Newstead civil team.  The role offers the opportunity to lead technical design, manage small-scale projects, and work on projects across our national portfolio.
You’ll enjoy working alongside respected industry professionals and possess the agility required to consistently deliver high-quality work across a diverse range of projects, including:
- Land Subdivisions
- Local Government Infrastructure & Urban Master Planning
- Stormwater, Flood Modelling & WSUD
- Aged Care, Childcare, Education and Retirement Living.
- Multi-Residential, Commercial & Industrial Developments
Requirements for Success
- 4 year Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering (Engineers Australia-recognised)
- At least 7 years of post-grad experience, ideally with some experience working on projects in SEQ, and requiring interactions with local government authorities and asset managers
- Strong technical design skills and proficiency with relevant software
- RPEQ, NER, or CPEng accreditation (or working towards it)
Why Westera Partners?
We offer a dynamic and collaborative work environment, where individual efforts are recognised and high performance is rewarded with competitive pay and the conditions to perform at your best.
Your drive to deliver outstanding services will be supported with plenty of formal and informal mentoring from industry leaders who genuinely care about you and your career aspirations. 
While we remain focused on delivering outstanding services to our clients, we also foster a culture that values work-life balance and individual wellbeing.
Regular social events and team gatherings provide opportunities to connect, celebrate achievements, and continuously improve. 
Join our team
We welcome applications from experienced civil design engineers who are driven and keen to deepen their expertise within a dynamic consultancy environment.  To be considered, you must be able to provide evidence of the following:
- Recent experience applying Australian design standards on projects delivered in SEQ
- 4-year degree qualification recognised by Engineers Australia (and RPEQ/NER/CPEng registration if applicable)
- Valid Australian Work Rights
- Valid Driver’s Licence
We’re excited about bringing a talented Civil Design Engineer onto the Westera team, so we will move quickly to interview candidates who demonstrate suitability. 
We look forward to hearing from you!
